name: Doom Wall
description: Everything for weight: the dist at its top, the low lifted all the way, the high down, and the middle lifted low, near 300 Hz. Slow, heavy chords.

name: Fizzy Bedroom
description: The dist at its top and the high all the way up: the buzzing top the pedal is mocked for, kept as it is. A cabinet or a high cut after it tames it.

name: Flat Noon
description: Every knob at its middle: the circuit's own voicing, the upper middle lifted before the clipping and the lows and the top lifted after it.

name: Hiss and All
description: The flat setting with the dist up and the pedal's own hiss turned on, for a part that should sound like a pedal on a floor.

name: Low Gain Crunch
description: The dist low, the equalizer near flat: chords that clip when they are hit and clean up a little as they fade, with the middle a touch forward.

name: Mid-Forward Lead
description: The middle lifted near 1.2 kHz and the dist well up, for single notes that sit in front of a band and sustain.

name: Scooped Classic
description: The sound the pedal is known for: the dist well up, the low and the high lifted, and the middle cut hard near 500 Hz. Chugging rhythm with the body taken out of the middle; into a clean amplifier or a cabinet.

name: Tight Modern
description: The dist high, the lows held back and the upper middle lifted near 2 kHz: palm-muted riffs that stay tight on a low string.
